title: Superintelligence and the Triple Risk of an AI Race
abstract: arXiv:2610.17085v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: On many estimates, artificial general intelligence (AGI) is likely to emerge within the next few decades or even sooner. Once it does, it may quickly surpass human intelligence, possibly by a huge margin. Some believe that the country that develops AGI first could attain global dominance. This prospect risks setting off intense competition between the United States and China. Indeed, a narrative has already developed that the superpowers are locked in an AI race, with the Trump administration proclaiming its determination to 'dismantle unnecessary regulatory barriers' to winning it. We argue that this approach presents three profound dangers. The first two are familiar from past arms races: being overtaken by a rival or triggering a war. The third is new: losing control of human beings' future to agents far more intelligent than we are, which could endanger our very survival. translated_title: 超级智能与人工智能竞赛的三重风险
translated_abstract: 根据许多估计，通用人工智能（AGI）很可能在未来几十年内甚至更早出现。一旦实现，它可能迅速超越人类智能，甚至可能以巨大的幅度领先。有人认为，率先开发出AGI的国家可以获得全球主导地位。这一前景可能引发中美之间的激烈竞争。事实上，“超级大国已陷入人工智能竞赛”的叙事已经形成，特朗普政府宣称决心“拆除不必要的监管壁垒”以赢得这场竞赛。我们认为这种做法蕴含着三重深刻的危险。前两个危险在过去的军备竞赛中已为人所熟知：被竞争对手超越，或引发战争。第三个危险则是全新的：将人类的未来拱手让给远比我们更智能的智能体，这可能危及人类自身的生存。争相率先实现AGI的做法可能导致安全方面的“逐底竞争”。
tldr: 本文指出中美为率先实现通用人工智能而展开的竞赛蕴含三重风险——被对手超越、引发战争，以及全新的、可能危及人类生存的风险：将人类未来失控于远超人类智能的超级智能体。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that the US-China race to achieve AGI first poses three profound dangers—being overtaken by a rival, triggering a war, and, uniquely, losing control of humanity's future to far more intelligent AI agents, which could endanger human survival itself.
